topics.lesson_subject: FIPS-CC boot lifecycle: CPU-jitter entropy, cryptographic self-tests, and certified-branch maintenance
topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FIPS-CC mode boot-time cryptographic self-test plus CPU-jitter entropy source; firmware branch and validation status remain separate lifecycle controls
topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: backup/configure FIPS-CC -> reboot -> run self-tests and seed RNG from CPU jitter -> verify self-test/firmware-integrity output -> maintain on matching FIPS-CC firmware branch
topics.failure_class: FIPS-CC boot/self-test or entropy-source incompatibility; wrong GA versus FIPS-CC image/branch selection
topics.evidence_pattern: FIPS-CC boot banner; per-algorithm self-test pass/fail lines; firmware integrity test; config system fips-cc status; release/readme build identity
topics.remediation_path: verify platform and branch eligibility; back up because enabling/disabling FIPS-CC is disruptive and can lose configuration; follow matching FIPS-CC build ReadMe; verify self-tests before returning traffic
topics.question_fingerprint: distinguish cryptographic self-test/entropy readiness from a firmware branch or certification claim
topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: boot sequence: firmware image -> FIPS-CC mode gate -> CPU-jitter RNG seed -> algorithm self-tests -> integrity check -> operational state
topics.scenario_status: Recent, directly relevant firmware-branch scenario; not a boot self-test failure case.

community_sweep.note: FIPS-CC/CVE-patched branch update; supports branch-maintenance lesson, not a self-test failure.

topics.lesson_subject: Firmware-template profile database: desired-version records, scheduled campaign state, hidden profiles, and safe ADOM-scoped cleanup
topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiManager firmware templates persist per-ADOM enforced-version and schedule profiles in an internal profile database; GUI visibility and cached scheduled profile records can diverge
topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: template desired versions/schedule stored per ADOM -> scheduler consumes profile -> diagnose fwmanager profile list exposes profile entries and checksums -> optional ADOM-scoped clear removes cached records -> verify list again
topics.failure_class: stale or orphaned scheduled firmware profile remains active although template is not visible in GUI; overbroad clear can remove profiles across every ADOM
topics.evidence_pattern: diagnose fwmanager profile list grouped by ADOM; profile name/oid/enforced version/schedule/checksum; GUI Firmware Templates inventory; task monitor scheduled job entries
topics.remediation_path: list profiles before and after; identify exact ADOM and profile; clear only that ADOM with diagnose fwmanager profile clear <ADOM_NAME>; never run unscoped clear without change approval and backup; re-create desired template and verify schedule
topics.question_fingerprint: recognize GUI-hidden scheduled firmware profile state and select a scoped rather than global cleanup operation
topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: per-ADOM firmware template GUI -> persistent profile database -> scheduler/task monitor -> firmware campaign; scoped cleanup isolates one ADOM
topics.scenario_status: Recent, directly relevant operational tip; the CLI cleanup command is scenario evidence, while template behavior is defined by the Administration Guide.

community_sweep.note: Firmware profile database list/clear procedure and ADOM scope.

topics.lesson_subject: Device Manager Up/Down state: OFTP connectivity, log-recency thresholds, and post-reboot reconciliation
topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: Device Manager status is derived from OFTP connection state and/or last-log-received freshness with separate near-real-time and scheduled-upload thresholds
topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: FortiGate OFTP reconnects and logs resume -> oftpd observes packets -> fortilogd ingests -> Device Manager recalculates status/last-log display on refresh cycle
topics.failure_class: false-down/stale-last-log after FortiAnalyzer reboot versus genuine transport, authorization, or log-ingestion failure
topics.evidence_pattern: FortiGate test-connectivity registered/up; oftpd device entry and increasing received packet count; fortilogd lograte; Device Manager last-log timestamp; 15-minute near-real-time and 6-hour scheduled-upload defaults
topics.remediation_path: allow 10-15 minute UI reconciliation window; if still down after 30 minutes inspect OFTP, port 514 path, registration/authorization, fortilogd, and release notes
topics.question_fingerprint: separate delayed UI state convergence from a real OFTP or log-ingestion outage using independent evidence
topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiGate OFTP/log stream -> FortiAnalyzer oftpd -> fortilogd -> Device Manager status evaluator -> GUI last-log/status view
topics.scenario_status: Recent, directly matched post-reboot status-convergence scenario.

community_sweep.note: Post-reboot Device Manager status lag and OFTP/log-rate verification.

topics.lesson_subject: SSH host-key regeneration after OpenSSH/firmware upgrade: trust negotiation, daemon restart, and managed-switch recovery
topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: SSH server host-key material and algorithm negotiation; execute ssh-regen-keys replaces host keys and restarts sshd
topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: client connects -> algorithm/host-key negotiation -> host authenticates server key -> user authentication; regeneration changes server identity and terminates active SSH sessions
topics.failure_class: host-key/algorithm negotiation failure or sshd crash after version-specific OpenSSH upgrade
topics.evidence_pattern: client_loop Broken pipe; SSH packet type 50/51 publickey trace; repeated /bin/sshd killed entries; known-host fingerprint mismatch; CLI command confirmation
topics.remediation_path: use console or supported alternate management path; execute ssh-regen-keys; accept/verify new host fingerprint on clients; disable temporary telnet access immediately; upgrade to fixed release where applicable
topics.question_fingerprint: distinguish server host-key negotiation failure from user credential failure and identify the safe recovery path
topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: SSH client -> FortiGate management proxy (optional) -> FortiSwitch sshd host-key negotiation -> regenerated key/fingerprint trust update
topics.scenario_status: Recent, directly matched version-specific failure; Fortinet states the 108-model issue is fixed in 7.6.9.

community_sweep.note: 108-series SSH daemon/key regeneration issue; outside rolling 30-day window.

topics.lesson_subject: Distributed Automatic Radio Resource Provisioning (DARRP): channel scoring, density profiles, monitor thresholds, and schedules
topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: DARRP selects channels using weighted RF observations (total RSSI, noise floor, channel load, spectral RSSI, retries/errors) and scheduled optimization/monitor windows
topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: FortiAP radios collect RF/channel measurements -> DARRP profile weights/thresholds score candidate channels -> scheduled optimizer chooses channel -> monitor interval observes retries/errors and may trigger reselection
topics.failure_class: suboptimal or unstable channel assignment from poor density profile, stale measurement window, DFS/weather-channel behavior, or excessive reselection thresholds
topics.evidence_pattern: DARRP profile assignment; selection-period and monitor-period; channel load/noise/spectral RSSI; TX retries/RX errors; schedule and channel-change events
topics.remediation_path: choose high/medium-density profile or tune weights with RF survey evidence; set realistic thresholds and optimization schedule; account for DFS/radar channels and channel width; capture client/AP logs during observed roaming issue
topics.question_fingerprint: choose whether a channel change is caused by candidate scoring, monitor-stage retry threshold, or schedule timing
topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: multiple FortiAP radios feed RF metric vectors into DARRP scoring/profile engine -> scheduled channel selector -> monitor feedback loop
topics.scenario_status: Related operational evidence guide; it is a troubleshooting collection article, not a DARRP feature specification.

community_sweep.note: Recent roaming evidence collection; related troubleshooting evidence, not DARRP feature specification.

topics.lesson_subject: Secure/static port enforcement: physical-address filtering, switch MAC-table visibility, and disabled-host persistence
topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiNAC Physical Address Filtering controls hosts through switch secure/static ports; model configuration tells L2 polling to read static MAC entries that are otherwise ignored
topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: enable secure-port capability in switch model -> L2 poll reads static MAC table -> FortiNAC maps MAC to host/port -> host disable action installs/remains as static disabled MAC on switch
topics.failure_class: connected hosts invisible to FortiNAC because secure-port MAC entries are static and omitted from normal L2 polling; disabled MAC persists after host record deletion
topics.evidence_pattern: switch MAC table shows STATIC instead of DYNAMIC; FortiNAC Ports View lacks host while L2 poll reports success; Model Configuration secure-port flag and ForwardTableStatic attribute
topics.remediation_path: enable Secure Ports is enabled for ports on this device in Model Configuration; set ForwardTableStatic true where required; run L2 Hosts Poll Now; verify Physical Address Filtering group and per-VLAN secure-port prerequisites
topics.question_fingerprint: distinguish a successful L2 poll from complete MAC visibility when switch port security converts learned entries to static entries
topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: secure switch port/static MAC table -> FortiNAC model capability -> L2 poll/host mapping -> physical-address filtering disable action
topics.scenario_status: Directly matched but old (September 28, 2018); used only as a mechanism example, not represented as a recent article.

community_sweep.note: Secure-port static-MAC polling visibility; direct mechanism but old.

topics.lesson_subject: Persistent Agent registry-key scans: hive selection, execution identity, severity, and remediation workflow
topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiNAC-F custom scan invokes Persistent Agent registry-key check against configured Windows hive/key; scan context runs under agent service identity, not interactive logged-on user
topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: create registry-key custom scan -> choose hive/key/value/type/operator and failure severity -> attach scan to general scan/endpoint compliance policy -> agent evaluates registry path -> pass/fail result returned to FortiNAC-F -> policy/remediation branch
topics.failure_class: false compliance failure when required registry value is in HKEY_CURRENT_USER, unavailable to the service identity, or incorrect hive/path/severity/OS applicability
topics.evidence_pattern: custom scan result label/severity; selected hive/key/value; agent log scan result; compare HKLM versus HKCU access under service identity; Windows OS applicability selection
topics.remediation_path: use machine-wide HKLM/HKEY_USERS locations for machine compliance; do not rely on HKCU when the agent runs as another user; validate key path, REG_DWORD decimal value, operator, OS applicability, and scan order before enforcing denial
topics.question_fingerprint: identify why a registry value exists for the interactive user but the Persistent Agent scan cannot read it
topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiNAC-F scan definition -> Persistent Agent service identity -> Windows registry hive/key/value -> scan result -> compliance policy/remediation branch
topics.scenario_status: Older related custom-scan scenario; it concerns certificate-store visibility, not registry-key scans.

community_sweep.note: Persistent Agent custom-scan certificate visibility; related, not registry-key scan.

topics.lesson_subject: Secure remote LDAP: LDAPS/StartTLS trust anchors, CRL validation depth, and optional mutual-TLS client identity
topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: remote LDAP connection TLS mode plus selected trusted CA and CRL scope; optional client certificate authenticates FAC to LDAP server
topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: FAC resolves LDAP FQDN -> TCP/636 LDAPS or StartTLS upgrade -> server certificate chain validation -> optional CRL checks at leaf/all chain nodes -> optional client-certificate auth -> LDAP bind/search/user sync
topics.failure_class: TLS certificate verification failure due missing intermediate/root, incomplete chain, expired/revoked certificate, CRL gap, or server-name mismatch
topics.evidence_pattern: FAC remote sync error SSL routines certificate verify failed/unable to get local issuer; packet capture TLS handshake; server-presented chain; trusted CA selection; CRL Check Mode; LDAP sync logs
topics.remediation_path: import complete trusted chain; verify server name/SAN and validity; choose Single CA or All Trusted deliberately; for All Nodes supply CRLs for each CA and full server chain; test LDAP browse/sync before changing user mapping
topics.question_fingerprint: determine whether LDAP bind failure is caused by TLS chain trust, CRL scope, client certificate, or LDAP credentials
topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiAuthenticator LDAP client -> TLS handshake/server chain validation -> optional CRL/OCSP decision -> optional client certificate -> LDAP bind/search
topics.scenario_status: Older contextual case (2025); directly illustrates missing intermediate CA and remote-sync TLS failure.

community_sweep.note: Remote LDAP sync certificate-chain verification failure.

topics.lesson_subject: Active-passive HA: configuration replication, primary-only audit/video persistence, heartbeat topology, and failover maintenance mode
topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: one active plus up to two passive FortiPAM nodes; configuration/users/secrets synchronize, but event logs and session videos remain on the node that recorded them
topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: primary handles all PAM tasks -> HA heartbeat and config sync to passive -> monitored-interface/primary failure -> passive takes primary role and enters maintenance mode -> administrator resumes services after recovery/maintenance action
topics.failure_class: HA sync failure from cross-platform/version/model mismatch, license SKU mismatch, file backup/sync error, heartbeat congestion, or data-retention expectation mismatch
topics.evidence_pattern: HA role/state/priority; hasync and hatalk debug; file synchronization failure paths; checksum/sync status; node serial owning log records; heartbeat packet path
topics.remediation_path: match model/version/platform and license SKU; verify dedicated heartbeat and monitored interfaces; test unicast heartbeat where multicast congestion exists; set priority/override separately on each node; design external log/video retention because data is not replicated
topics.question_fingerprint: identify which FortiPAM state survives failover and which audit/video artifacts remain tied to the original primary
topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: active FortiPAM node with configuration sync to two passive nodes; separate unsynchronized local log/video stores; heartbeat and monitored data interfaces
topics.scenario_status: Older operational case (about six months); useful for file-sync, platform, license-SKU, and heartbeat diagnosis.

community_sweep.note: HA file synchronization, platform, license, and heartbeat troubleshooting.

topics.lesson_subject: Windows Event Forwarding (WEF): source-initiated subscription, centralized agent collection, and original-host attribution
topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: Windows Event Sources push selected Windows Security/Application/System events to a central Windows Event Collector; one FortiSIEM Windows Agent on WEC forwards ForwardedEvents while parser fields preserve original source identity
topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: source-initiated WEF subscription -> WinRM/WEC accepts event source -> source pushes event to ForwardedEvents log -> FortiSIEM Agent reads ForwardedEvents -> Collector parses XML/event fields -> Analytics retains original reporting host attributes while CMDB source is WEF host
topics.failure_class: events absent due WinRM/WEC subscription or firewall/ACL problem; source identity appears as WEF server because parser/template/source fields are misinterpreted; unsupported event channels assumed to be forwarded
topics.evidence_pattern: wecutil subscription runtime status; Event Viewer ForwardedEvents entries; Windows Agent template event name ForwardedEvents (case-sensitive); Include Events ALL/Exclude NONE; parsed SourceHostName/Reporting Host and event source fields
topics.remediation_path: configure WinRM and Windows Event Collector on WEC; create source-initiated subscription and source authorization; install FortiSIEM Agent only on WEC; configure ForwardedEvents case-sensitively; verify original host attributes in parsed events; use native agents for FIM/Sysmon/custom data not covered by WEF
topics.question_fingerprint: separate WEF transport source/CMDB identity from original reporting host attributes inside the forwarded event
topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: many Windows source computers -> source-initiated WEF/WinRM subscriptions -> central WEC ForwardedEvents log -> single FortiSIEM Agent -> Collector parser -> Analytics source attributes
topics.scenario_status: Older contextual case (June 2026); directly explains CMDB source identity versus original event source attributes.

community_sweep.note: WEF/WEC source identity and ForwardedEvents collection.

topics.lesson_subject: Agentless explicit proxy and SIA tunnel mutual exclusion: port 9443, SNI rewrite, and domain-fronting 403
topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: agentless PAC/explicit proxy path and agent-based SIA tunnel are distinct access modes; proxy changes SNI and cannot be layered concurrently with SIA tunnel for same flow
topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: browser PAC/proxy selects FortiSASE proxy endpoint (default 9443) -> proxy applies web policy and modifies SNI -> endpoint SIA tunnel simultaneously encapsulates traffic -> FortiSASE domain-fronting control rejects conflicting SNI/tunnel path
topics.failure_class: 403 domain-fronting block caused by dual steering/proxy+tunnel path and SNI mismatch, not destination website availability
topics.evidence_pattern: browser DevTools shows proxy port 9443 rather than direct HTTPS 443; endpoint proxy settings/PAC; SIA tunnel state; HTTP 403 domain-fronting blocked; SNI seen on tunneled flow
topics.remediation_path: choose one access mode per endpoint/traffic flow; disable endpoint proxy/PAC when using SIA tunnel or remove tunnel for agentless proxy use; verify DNS/PAC and SNI path after change
topics.question_fingerprint: identify the duplicate steering path from port/SNI evidence and select the mutually exclusive access mode
topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: endpoint browser PAC/proxy and FortiClient SIA tunnel as parallel mutually exclusive paths to FortiSASE PoP; conflict converges at SNI/domain-fronting gate
topics.scenario_status: Recent, directly matched operational scenario with port 9443 and SNI evidence.

community_sweep.note: 403 domain-fronting block caused by explicit proxy and SIA tunnel conflict.

topics.lesson_subject: Remote-health-check BGP route suppression when every hub-to-spoke overlay is dead: MED failover across dual hubs
topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: remote-SLA-probe all-member-dead state -> dynamic BGP route suppression -> outbound route-map matches suppress flag -> MED raised to 999 so alternate hub wins; distinct from route-tag destination classification and cloud connector address matching
topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: spoke emits remote SLA probes across hub overlay members -> hub counts alive members -> when all are dead, health-check update-bgp-route marks spoke route suppressed -> outbound route-map match-suppress sets high MED and neighbor preserves MED -> remote peer selects alternate hub -> recovery restores normal MED after probes return
topics.failure_class: blackhole through preferred hub after every overlay tunnel to a spoke has failed but BGP route remains advertised with preferred metric
topics.evidence_pattern: diagnose sys sdwan health-check remote; diagnose sys link-monitor dynamic-bgp-peers showing alive-count and route-suppressed; get router info bgp network <prefix> showing alternate paths and MED; packet capture showing selected alternate overlay
topics.remediation_path: enable update-bgp-route on the remote health-check; match suppression in route-map-out; set high MED for suppressed and lower MED for normal; preserve MED toward external peers; tune failtime/recoverytime and validate both hubs before rollout
topics.question_fingerprint: distinguish one failed overlay member from all-member remote probe failure and identify the MED change that moves traffic to the alternate hub
topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: dual hub / dual spoke overlay; remote probe fan-out; alive-count gate; suppressed-route state; outbound BGP route-map MED rewrite; alternate hub best path
topics.scenario_status: No directly matched recent Community troubleshooting scenario verified; the Fortinet feature guide includes a full dual-hub failure and failover example.

community_sweep.note: No directly matched Community scenario verified; official feature guide supplies a dual-hub failover example.
